story.originalTitle: Hamilton 'devastated', Leclerc 'angry' after Ferrari Las Vegas shocker
story.summaryEn: Both Ferrari drivers, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, were eliminated in Q2 during Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying, with Leclerc saying he was "angry" and Hamilton saying he was "devastated." Leclerc will start the race from 10th, with Hamilton one place behind him.
detailZh: 拉斯维加斯大奖赛：法拉利两位车手在排位赛中双双意外早早出局后，刘易斯·汉密尔顿表示“极度沮丧”，夏尔·勒克莱尔则感到“愤怒”。
夏尔·勒克莱尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿在拉斯维加斯排位赛的Q2双双被淘汰；勒克莱尔将从第10位发车，汉密尔顿排在他身后一位；周日的正赛将于凌晨4点开始（凌晨2点30分开始预热），在天空体育F1频道和Main Event频道直播。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔在Q2双双被淘汰，法拉利在拉斯维加斯排位赛中倍感沮丧。
夏尔·勒克莱尔感到“愤怒”，刘易斯·汉密尔顿则表示自己“极度沮丧”，此前法拉利两位车手在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中双双意外早早出局。
这支意大利车队抵达拉斯维加斯大道赛道时，对长直道和低温可能带来的挑战心存警惕，但周五晚上的练习与排位比两位车手预想的还要糟糕得多。
两位车手都在第二节排位赛中被淘汰，勒克莱尔以第11名完赛，汉密尔顿紧随其后位列第12。由于迈凯伦车手奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里受罚，他们将在正赛发车格上各前进一位。

勒克莱尔似乎拥有足够的速度进入Q3，但他在最后一圈飞驰圈中犯了错误。这位摩纳哥车手对法拉利感到愤怒，因为车队没有给他留出足够的时间，以便在出现失误或问题时再跑一圈。
“是的，当然（Q3是有可能的），但我们做得不好，”勒克莱尔告诉天空体育F1。
“基本上，在我唯一被给予的那一圈里，我犯了一个错误。”

“与此同时，执行做得非常糟糕。我不知道。我们会复盘。”
“我现在非常生气，所以宁愿不多说。但我认为有很多事情我们本可以做得更好。”
“极度沮丧”的汉密尔顿透露了赛车损伤和能量部署问题
汉密尔顿在整个练习阶段都缺乏速度，他表示这是由于他在早期阶段对自己的赛车造成了损伤。
“我很沮丧，”汉密尔顿告诉天空体育F1频道。“我们努力做好工作。
“我其实不太清楚我们今天会处在什么位置。我们知道在这些长直道上我们会有些吃力，但我进入时是乐观的，我以为赛车会没问题。
“但在第一圈或第二圈，我们的底板被什么东西撞了一下，一些碎片或其他东西损坏了底板，我们因此损失了大量下压力，大约零点几秒。
法拉利车手刘易斯·汉密尔顿在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中仅列第12位，赛后感到十分沮丧。
与勒克莱尔不同，汉密尔顿在Q2末尾成功完成了一个飞驰圈，但他表示，一个能量部署问题几乎断送了他晋级的机会。
“然后我倾尽了全力，”他补充道。“我那圈在最后已经做到了最好，但我前面没有车，接着我们在最后阶段出现了能量部署不足，光在部署上我就损失了大约0.6秒。
“祸不单行。今天就是这样的日子。
“我们当时拼尽全力只想进入第三节排位赛。我认为如果没有部署损失，没有下压力损失，我本可以进入第三节排位赛，但那仍然会很艰难。”
“但事已至此，已经结束了。对整个车队来说这绝对不是什么好受的感觉，但我们明天会努力向前看。”
勒克莱尔对法拉利在正赛中的前景感到沮丧，正赛将于周日凌晨4点在天空体育F1频道直播，他坚称车队缺乏直线速度会让他很难向前推进。
当被问及反击的可能性时，他说：“我不这么认为，因为我们在直道上损失了一秒，所以 literally 我们没有任何地方能够超车。”
安东内利在排位赛中跑出最快圈速，但马克斯·维斯塔潘将从头名发车，因为梅赛德斯为安东内利更换了本赛季第六台内燃机，他将在拉斯维加斯大奖赛上接受五位发车位罚退。
天空体育F1评论员杰米·查德威克表示，她能理解两位车手为何会对车队在排位赛中的执行感到沮丧。
查德威克说：“我不理解的一点是，我认为这正是查尔斯所指的执行问题，他在最后一圈没有任何犯错余地。这让他很沮丧。
“而在刘易斯这边，他始终是孤军奋战。如果他们说在直道上损失了一秒，那至少应该设法创造有利条件，利用尾流给自己最好的机会。”

detailEn: Las Vegas GP: Lewis Hamilton 'devastated' and Charles Leclerc 'angry' after both Ferrari drivers make shock early exits from qualifying

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were both eliminated from Q2 during qualifying in Las Vegas; Leclerc will start the race from 10th, with Hamilton a place behind him; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were eliminated from Q2 as Ferrari were left frustrated in Las Vegas qualifying
Charles Leclerc was left "angry" while Lewis Hamilton said he was "devastated" after both Ferrari drivers suffered shock early exits from Las Vegas Grand Prix Qualifying.

The Italian team had arrived at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit wary of the challenges the long straights and cold temperatures could pose them, but Friday night's session went far worse than either driver had anticipated.
Both drivers were eliminated in Q2 as Leclerc took 11th with Hamilton a place behind him. They will each move a position forward on the grid due to a penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

Leclerc appeared to have more than enough pace to reach Q3 but made a mistake on his final flying lap. The Monegasque was infuriated by Ferrari not having left him enough time to go for another lap in the event of an error or issue.
"Yes, for sure (Q3 was on the cards) but we didn't do a good job," Leclerc told Sky Sports F1.
"I did a mistake the only lap I was given, basically.
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix
"And at the same time, the execution has been very poor. I don't know. We'll review.
"I'm very angry now, so I would rather not speak too much. But I think there were plenty of things we could have done much better."
'Devastated' Hamilton reveals damage and deployment issues
Hamilton was lacking pace throughout the session, which he suggested was caused by damage he had done to his car in the early stages.
"I'm devastated," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1. "We work hard to do a good job.
"I didn't really know where we were going to be today. We knew we would struggle a little bit with these long straights, but I was optimistic going in, I thought the car would be OK.
"But on the first or second lap, we took a hit from something on the floor, some debris or something damaged the floor and we lost a bunch of downforce with it, a few tenths."
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated after he could only qualify 12th for the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Unlike Leclerc, Hamilton was able to get a flying lap in at the end of Q2, but he said a deployment issue all but ended his hopes of advancing.

"And then I was giving it everything," he added. "My lap was as good as it could be at the end, but I didn't have anyone ahead of me, and then we had a lack of deployment at the end and I lost like six tenths just on deployment.
"When it rains it pours. It was just one of those days.
"We were scrapping to just get into Q3. I think without the deployment loss, without the downforce loss, I think I could have got into Q3, but it would have still been tough.
"But it is what is, it's over. It's definitely not a nice feeling for all the team, but we'll try to move forwards tomorrow."

Leclerc was downcast over Ferrari's prospects for the race, which is live on Sky Sports F1 at 4am on Sunday morning, insisting their lack of straight-line speed would make it difficult for him to move forward.
Asked about the prospect of a fightback, he said: "I don't think so because we are losing a second down the straights, so there is literally nowhere we will be able to overtake."

Kimi Antonelli went fastest in qualifying but Max Verstappen will start on pole as Antonelli will serve a five-place grid penalty for the Las Vegas Grand Prix after Mercedes fitted his sixth internal combustion engine of the season
Sky Sports F1 pundit Jamie Chadwick said she could understand why both drivers would be frustrated by the team's execution during qualifying.
Chadwick said: "The thing that I don't understand, and I think this is where Charles refers to the execution, he had no margin to make a mistake on that last lap. That's frustrating for him.

"And then on Lewis' side, he was always on his own. If they're saying that they're losing a second on the straight, at least stack the odds in your favour to have a slipstream and give yourself the best chance."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

法拉利在查尔斯·勒克莱尔发生打滑和刘易斯·汉密尔顿出现引擎问题后，周五的比赛非常艰难，但勒克莱尔在最终练习中表现更好，排在第五位，领先于迈凯轮的兰多·诺里斯和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里。
汉密尔顿在整个练习赛中都很不高兴，并在他的最后一圈飞驰后表示他的“赛车无法转向”，这使他排在第九位，位于小红牛车队的Arvid Lindblad和劳森之间。

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
